findings.issue: The compiler's zeroed struct-array allocation has its first two elements peeled before a count-down 'while idx - 1', and the ABI encoding of the result is rotated in one arm (first element encoded before the shared loop, which then starts at a phi'd index), so the return length becomes '_94 - 96 * _97 + 96 * max(_95, _97) - mem[64]'.
findings.rule: Re-roll peeled iterations that are equal to the loop body up to the induction variable (the loop then starts at 0 and the phi of its start disappears); with the start index constant the length folds to 96 * n + 64.

findings.source: OZ AccessControlUpgradeable._checkRole -> StringsUpgradeable.toHexString: for (uint256 i = 2 * length + 1; i > 1; --i) { buffer[i] = _SYMBOLS[value & 0xf]; value >>= 4; }
findings.issue: The loop itself is readable (and the '0x' prefix is folded into the message), but each copy keeps the bounds check of buffer[i] although i <= 2 * length + 1 < buffer.length on every iteration (52 copies).
findings.rule: A bounds check 'i >= n' inside a loop whose induction variable starts at n - 1 and only decreases is false; drop it.

notes: All 60 ABI functions and the fallback reviewed; no semantic error found. Small getters, role management (OZ AccessControl with the toHexString revert message), pause/unpause, flow-rate setters read directly; deposit / depositTo / depositETH / depositToETH / mapToken / onMessageReceive / finaliseQueuedWithdrawal(s) / findPendingWithdrawals / getPendingWithdrawals by structure (token mapping checks, IMX cumulative limit, message encoding to the bridge adaptor with value, flow-rate bucket updates and queue activation, withdrawal queue entries, events). Source loops: toHexString (inlined 52 times), getPendingWithdrawals, findPendingWithdrawals' search loop (a flag-driven 'while _47' with the '&&' condition recomputed at the end of the body, readable) and its copy loop, finaliseQueuedWithdrawalsAggregated's loop: all whiles. Implicit: struct-array zero allocations (rotated, P3), name/symbol string decodings and the message ABI encodings (19 plain copies, P7). The second initialize overload always reverts with 0xf0e22197 (WrongInitializer), as in the source.
summary: Faithful; every source loop is a readable while (the toHexString loops even fold the '0x' prefix into the message); the remaining obscurity is the compiler's peeled struct-array allocations and rotated result encodings in the withdrawal-queue views.
